data.name: Jal
data.gender_notes: Jal is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘jalila’, meaning to be gentle and kind. In Islamic history, Jal refers to a gentle and compassionate Prophet. This name is a reminder of the importance of being kind and compassionate in our daily lives. The name Jal carries the meaning “Gentle, kind” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Jal usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle, kind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jal belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle, kind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jal total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Jalaluddin Muhammad Rumi was a 13th century Persian poet, jurist, theologian, and Sufi mystic. He is known as Rumi because of his Mevlevi nickname 'Mevlana', meaning 'our master' or 'our respected one'.
historical_references.context: Rumi's poetry has been widely read and loved for its depth of spiritual insight, its musicality, its close connection to the Sufi tradition, and its emphasis on love, self-surrender, and the longing for ecstatic union with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Sultan Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Akbar was a 16th century Mughal Emperor of India. He is considered the greatest of the Mughal emperors and is renowned for his military conquests, architectural achievements, and religious tolerance.
historical_references.context: Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Akbar was given the name 'Jalal' as a title, meaning 'radiant' or 'majestic'. He established a new capital at Fatehpur Sikri and built many magnificent structures, including the Taj Mahal, which remains one of the most famous architectural landmarks in the world.
